## Construction

Let $\varphi = \frac{1+\sqrt5}{2}$, let $\{t\} = t - \lfloor t\rfloor$ denote the fractional part, and define

$$x_n = 3\{n\varphi\}, \qquad n \ge 0.$$

Since $0 \le \{n\varphi\} < 1$, we have $|x_n| \le 3$, so the sequence is bounded.

## Key lemma

For every integer $q \ge 1$, $\; q\,\|q\varphi\| \ge \tfrac13$, where $\|t\|$ is the distance from $t$ to the nearest integer.

**Proof.** Let $p$ be an integer nearest to $q\varphi$, and set $\delta = q\varphi - p$, so $|\delta| = \|q\varphi\| \le \tfrac12$. Let $\varphi' = \frac{1-\sqrt5}{2} = 1-\varphi$ be the conjugate of $\varphi$. Then

$$(p - q\varphi)(p - q\varphi') = p^2 - pq - q^2,$$

which is a nonzero integer because $\varphi$ is irrational and $(p,q)\neq(0,0)$. Hence $|p - q\varphi|\cdot|p - q\varphi'| \ge 1$.

Now bound the second factor. Since $|p| \le q\varphi + \tfrac12$ and $|\varphi'| < 0.62$,

$$|p - q\varphi'| \le q\varphi + \tfrac12 + 0.62\,q \le \sqrt5\,q + \tfrac12.$$

Therefore $|\delta| \ge \dfrac{1}{\sqrt5\,q + \frac12}$, and so

$$q|\delta| \ge \frac{q}{\sqrt5\,q + \frac12} \ge \frac13,$$

where the last inequality is equivalent to $(3-\sqrt5)\,q \ge \tfrac12$. This holds for all $q\ge 1$ since $3-\sqrt5 \approx 0.764$. $\blacksquare$

## Verification

Take distinct $i, j \ge 0$ and let $d = i - j \neq 0$. Then

$$x_i - x_j = 3(\{i\varphi\} - \{j\varphi\}) = 3(d\varphi - m)$$

for some integer $m$. So $|x_i - x_j| \ge 3\|d\varphi\| = 3\|\,|d|\varphi\|$. By the lemma with $q = |d|$,

$$|x_i - x_j| \ge \frac{3}{3|d|} = \frac{1}{|d|}.$$

Since $a > 1$ and $|d| \ge 1$,

$$|x_i - x_j|\,|i-j|^a \ge \frac{|d|^a}{|d|} = |d|^{a-1} \ge 1.$$

This holds for every pair of distinct nonnegative integers $i, j$, so the sequence satisfies the requirement.

ANSWER: $x_n = 3\{n\varphi\}$ with $\varphi=\frac{1+\sqrt5}{2}$ and $\{\cdot\}$ the fractional part, so $|x_n|\le 3$ and $|x_i-x_j|\,|i-j|^a\ge 1$.
